sources.entry: SnapOtter - Suite of 200+ web tools for converting and editing images, videos, audio and PDFs, including a layer-based image editor, OCR, transcription, background removal and batch processing pipelines (alternative to SmallPDF, iLovePDF, CloudConvert). (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: SnapOtter is a self-hosted, Docker-deployed suite of 200+ web tools for converting, compressing, editing, OCR-ing and transcribing images, video, audio, PDFs and documents, with a UI, REST API and pipelines.
summary.what_it_does: Provides roughly 200 file-processing tools grouped into image (112), video (57), audio (27), PDF (35) and files (23) categories, covering conversion, compression, resizing, trimming, merging, watermarking and similar edits. Includes a browser-based layer image editor with brushes, shapes, adjustments and filters. Local AI features cover background removal, upscaling, photo restoration, object erasing, face blurring, OCR for images and PDFs, audio transcription and auto-generated video subtitles, all run on the user's own hardware. Tools can be chained into reusable pipelines (JSON import/export) and batch-processed, and every tool is exposed through a REST API with API-key auth and interactive docs at /api/docs. The README says files are not sent to external services, though basic analytics are on by default and can be disabled.
use_cases: convert image or video formats on a home server
compress and resize photos in batches
merge, split, or redact PDFs without uploading to a third party
automate file processing through a REST API
how_to_run: Open http://localhost:1349 and log in with admin / admin (password change required on first login)
For production: save the README's compose.yaml (app + Postgres 17 + Redis 8) and run docker compose up -d
For NVIDIA GPU acceleration, use the GPU Compose file described in Docker Tags
stack: Node/TypeScript (inferred from REST API and build references is not stated; omitted)
notable: Single 'docker run' quick start with embedded Postgres and Redis, or a 3-container Compose stack for production
Covers five file modalities (image, video, audio, PDF, documents) in one stack, with local AI features
Pipelines chain tools into reusable workflows; batch size unlimited in the published image
OIDC/SSO login with Google, GitHub, Okta or any OpenID Connect provider
Multi-arch images for AMD64 and ARM64; 21 UI languages
caveats: Default admin/admin credentials; the Postgres example password must be changed for non-local deployments
Intel/AMD iGPU acceleration is not supported for AI inference; those systems run AI on CPU
Dual-licensed: AGPLv3 for free use, with a paid commercial license for proprietary or SaaS use
keywords: convert files on my own server
